A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain complete Appendices A–D. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison after matching material across formatting changes and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original Hamiltonian-cycle experiments, controlled Persona experiments, and reward-model evaluations on chat, math, and code data, including supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and additionally reports manual and automated validation of paraphrased responses in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: The EX-RM, IM-RM, and EX-GRM parameterizations, reward computations, objectives, and training procedures are retained. Expanded explanations and revised prompt-placeholder notation do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Hamiltonian-cycle verification, Persona, UltraFeedback and its paraphrased/French/Spanish variants, RewardMATH, and RewardBench math/code coverage. The new audit examines existing paraphrases without expanding reward-model task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain EX-RMs, IM-RMs, EX-GRMs, and Figure 7's all-representations and reference-free variants. GPT-5 mini is introduced as a paraphrase validator, not a competing reward model. Table 10 corrects a comparator header without changing the evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a validation protocol: manually examine 40 randomly selected paraphrased responses and use GPT-5 mini to assess semantic equivalence for all 400 responses. Existing reward-model splits, preprocessing, training budgets, and evaluation metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds an audit testing whether UltraFeedback paraphrases preserve meaning, including examination of a failed paraphrase. Existing hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, alternative-explanation tests, and controlled analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-seed reporting and standard deviations or error bars. The new paraphrase audit reports counts and proportions without introducing uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or repeated-run methodology.

E6.justification: Appendix D.3 newly reports that 39 of 40 manually reviewed paraphrases were valid and that GPT-5 mini flagged 9 of 400 responses (2.25%) as potentially invalid. Existing benchmark scores, plotted findings, and numerical table entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, Corollary 1, Assumptions 1–3, and the derivations and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged. Section 4.1 expands explanations of existing mathematics and moves the coefficient-positivity argument from a footnote into the text; it establishes no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that IM-RMs rely more on superficial token cues and that learning to verify need not require learning to generate. The new audit supplies supporting evidence without changing these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1's new footnote discusses architecture-dependent terms arising when hidden representations are trained and argues that existing experiments support persistence of the identified mechanism. Appendix D.3 additionally identifies prompts requiring a unique correct response as a paraphrasing failure case.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the new validator's exact model version, gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07, and its complete validation prompt, including the requested JSON output. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and Section 6 retains the same positioning relative to reward-model analysis, DPO versus RLHF, and implicit-bias research. Removing repeated citations in Section 2.1 does not change that positioning.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites and expands the coefficient explanation in Section 4.1, abbreviates several headings, and makes small abstract, introduction, and conclusion edits. The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICLR typography and headers, reflows figures and tables, and adds a validator-prompt box. Table 10's absolute-reward-margin header changes from EX-RM to EX-GRM, consistent with its existing caption and results. Plot contents and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides no direct validity audit of its generated paraphrases; v3 adds manual and automated checks with a reproducible validator prompt, modestly strengthening confidence in the token-level-shift evaluation. The clearer dynamics discussion and corrected Table 10 header also help. The gain is limited: benchmark results and formal guarantees remain unchanged, and no sensitivity rerun excluding flagged paraphrases is reported.
